note: Machine-readable compatibility ledger: every compatibility scenario is tracked as pass / known-gap / not-applicable under a permanent hc-<suite>-<capability>-<case> id. Status, reason and recordedAt semantics follow ADR-0002 section 7; the ledger was established by T11 and absorbed the T09 known-gap records (tests/compat/types/expected-divergences.json).

entries.reason: Since T22, MAD DOM's createWindow() succeeds, but the Window/Document facade only forwards lifecycle — the node surface (createElement, createTextNode, body, serialization) is not implemented yet, so the mad-dom side records a facade-phase TypeError while the happy-dom side records the full observation. First presented by the T10 real-pair runner; updated by T22; collected into the compatibility ledger by T11.

Since T22, MAD DOM's createWindow() succeeds, but the Window/Document facade lacks the node surface (body, querySelectorAll, getElementById, events), so the mad-dom side records a facade-phase TypeError while the happy-dom side records the full observation. First presented by the T10 real-pair runner; updated by T22; collected into the compatibility ledger by T11.

MAD DOM still does not export CSSRule or EventPhaseEnum, and its Window is not user-constructible (it needs a genuine native handle) while its Document lacks the node surface: tag-name overloads and NodeList iteration cannot be checked yet. Updated by T22 when Window became an exported, non-constructible class.

MAD DOM still does not export Event or EventPhaseEnum, and its Window is not user-constructible while its Document lacks addEventListener: listener parameter typing and enum comparison in event handlers cannot be checked yet. Updated by T22 when Window became an exported, non-constructible class.

MAD DOM does not export CustomEvent, and its Window is not user-constructible: the option-object constructor signature and the DetachedWindowAPI accessor are rejected. Updated by T22 when Window became an exported, non-constructible class.

MAD DOM does not export the Event value or the IEventInit/TEventListener type exports; annotations that reference them degrade to implicit any (TS7006) while the module-level gap exists. First recorded in T09 as div-types-type-exports; migrated into the compatibility ledger by T11.

MAD DOM's Window is not user-constructible (it requires a genuine native handle) and its Document lacks the node surface (createElement, querySelectorAll, title, body): the happy-dom-style window/double construction and element basics are rejected on the mad-dom target. Updated by T22 when Window became an exported, non-constructible class.
